# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER — Norwegian Listening Pod (15 Scenes)

## 1. TRANSLITERATION
Not needed — names stay as written. Norwegian uses Latin script exclusively.

## 2. PRICES
- Eight pound forty → hundre og tjuefem kroner
- Twelve pound fifty → hundreåtti kroner

## 3. TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME
Norwegian = *norsk*

## 4. RECURRING LINES

| Canonical | Norwegian (verbatim reuse) |
|-----------|---------------------------|
| Good morning. | God morgen. |
| Good afternoon. | God ettermiddag. |
| Good evening. | God kveld. |
| What can I get you? | Hva skal det være? |
| Thank you / Thank you very much. | Takk / Takk skal du ha. |
| Goodbye. | Ha det. / Ha det bra. |
| See you later / See you then. | Vi ses. |
| Excuse me. | Unnskyld. |
| Please. | Vær så snill. |
| Yes, of course. | Ja, selvfølgelig. |
| Could I pay by card? | Kan jeg betale med kort? |
| Do you have contactless? | Har dere kontaktløs? |
| Would you like to sit-in or takeaway? | Skal det være her eller med seg? |
| I'm learning Norwegian. | Jeg lærer norsk. |
| Could you say that again more slowly? | Kan du gjenta det litt saktere? |
| Pleased to meet you. | Hyggelig å møte deg. |
| Where are you from? | Hvor er du fra? |
| What do you do? | Hva jobber du som? / Hva gjør du? |
| I'm on holiday here. | Jeg er på ferie her. |

## 5. REGISTER

**Across all scenes: *du* throughout.** Politeness is marked by tone and phrasing (one well-placed *takk*, a simple *vær så snill* where appropriate), not grammatical honorifics. No *De*, no archaic forms. Staff to customers, strangers to each other, friends to learner — all *du*.
